shields.description: Shields are the primary defense of starships. Each ship is surrounded by 6 shields, each protecting a separate 60-degree arc (hex side). Shields absorb damage before it reaches the ship's internal systems.

shieldDirections.numbering: Shields are numbered 1 through 6, starting from the front (Shield 1) and proceeding clockwise. Shield 4 is the rear shield.

directions.name: Front
directions.description: Strongest shield, typically has the most boxes. Faces the ship's current heading.

directions.name: Rear
directions.description: Weakest shield typically. Faces directly behind the ship.

shieldDamage.description: When weapons fire hits a shield, damage points are subtracted from the shield's boxes. Each box represents one point of shield strength.
shieldDamage.resolution: Damage is applied to the shield facing the attacker. If the attacker is between two shields, a die roll determines which shield is hit.
shieldDamage.downedShield: When all boxes in a shield are marked out, the shield is 'down.' Further damage from that direction is allocated to the ship's internal systems via the Damage Allocation Chart.

shieldReinforcement.description: Players can allocate energy to reinforce shields, absorbing damage points and preventing them from marking out boxes on the SSD.
shieldReinforcement.requirement: Shields must be activated to use reinforcement.

types.description: Points are distributed to all shields and eliminated by the first damage from any direction.
Points are assigned to specific shields. More efficient than general reinforcement.

shieldReinforcement.restriction: Cannot reinforce shields in a nebula.

shieldRepair.description: Shields can be repaired during the game using Damage Control (DamCon) capability.

damageControl.description: The Damage Control rating is the highest undestroyed box on the DamCon track of the SSD.
damageControl.repairRate: DamCon rating determines how many shield points can be repaired per turn.
damageControl.repairLimit: Repairs are limited by the ship's current DamCon rating, which decreases as damage control systems are destroyed.

shieldRegeneration.description: Some ships have shield regeneration systems that automatically restore shield points over time.

shieldActivation.description: Shields must be activated to function. Activation requires energy allocation.

droppingShields.description: A player may voluntarily drop a specific shield to facilitate transporter use.
droppingShields.duration: A dropped shield must remain down for 1/4 of a turn (8 impulses), even if this extends into the next turn.

tacticalNotes: Maneuvering to present weaker shields to attackers is a key tactical consideration.
Turning to present fresh (undamaged) shields to incoming fire is a common tactic.
The front shield (Shield 1) typically has the most boxes, making head-on approaches difficult.
Attacking from the rear (Shield 4) is often the most effective approach.
